themes_detail.label: Illegal Posting Explosion
themes_detail.summary: Illegal posting complaints surged to 3 this week versus a baseline of 0.1 per week over the prior 8 weeks—a 2,300% spike (z-score: 8.69)—suggesting a sudden coordinated campaign or enforcement gap in Central Harlem that emerged THIS WEEK.
evidence: 3 illegal posting complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (2,300% increase)
Z-score of 8.69 indicates statistically extreme anomaly
Sharp single-week spike suggests sudden event or policy change rather than gradual trend
reporting_angles: Canvass the district to identify what is being posted and whether it is linked to a specific campaign, protest, or business
Contact 311 and Department of Sanitation to understand what triggered the spike and whether enforcement is responding

themes_detail.label: Graffiti Surge in Harlem
themes_detail.summary: Graffiti complaints jumped to 6 this week compared to a baseline of 0.8 per week—a 700% spike (z-score: 6.33)—indicating a THIS WEEK emergence of a street defacement problem worth investigating for gang activity, youth involvement, or territorial claims.
evidence: 6 graffiti complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.8 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (700% increase)
Z-score of 6.33 indicates highly significant anomaly
Timing aligns with illegal posting spike, suggesting possible coordinated street-level activity
reporting_angles: Map the specific locations of graffiti reports and check for tags, symbols, or messaging patterns that suggest organized activity
Interview NYPD and community groups about any known gang activity or youth group territorial disputes in the area

themes_detail.label: Street Vendor Crackdown Activity
themes_detail.summary: Vendor enforcement complaints spiked to 5 last week versus a baseline of 0.5 per week—a 900% increase (z-score: 5.2)—signaling either aggressive city enforcement action or a sudden influx of unlicensed vendors over the PAST 2 WEEKS.
evidence: 5 vendor enforcement complaints last week vs. 0.5 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (900% increase)
Z-score of 5.2 indicates statistically severe anomaly
Spike is 1 week old, making it recent enough to warrant immediate investigation
reporting_angles: Interview street vendors and local business owners to understand whether this is new enforcement targeting or a surge in unlicensed activity
Request data from Department of Consumer Affairs on enforcement sweeps or policy changes initiated in early April 2026

themes_detail.label: Sidewalk Deterioration Complaints
themes_detail.summary: Sidewalk condition complaints doubled to 10 this week from a baseline of 4.8 per week—a 110% increase (z-score: 2.83)—suggesting a THIS WEEK emergence of trip hazards, uneven pavement, or other pedestrian safety issues in Central Harlem.
evidence: 10 sidewalk condition complaints THIS WEEK vs. 4.8 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (110% increase)
Z-score of 2.83 exceeds 2.0 threshold for statistical significance
Complements other street-level concerns (illegal posting, graffiti) suggesting broader public space degradation this week
reporting_angles: Photograph the specific complaint locations to assess severity and liability risk to pedestrians, especially elderly and disabled residents
Track Department of Environmental Protection repair timelines to see if response capacity is being overwhelmed

themes_detail.label: Residential Noise Decline (Countertrend)
themes_detail.summary: Residential noise complaints dropped 23% to 201 this week from a baseline of 260.8 per week (z-score: -3.7)—a statistically significant REVERSAL of what is normally the #2 complaint type in Harlem, possibly indicating underreporting or a shift in resident behavior THIS WEEK.
evidence: 201 residential noise complaints THIS WEEK vs. 260.8 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (23% decrease, z-score: -3.7)
Countertrend is statistically significant, ruling out normal fluctuation
Timing coincides with other anomalies (illegal posting, graffiti) but in opposite direction, warranting investigation
reporting_angles: Check whether a major event, holiday, or policy change occurred this week that reduced foot traffic or late-night activity
Verify whether 311 portal experienced technical issues that may have reduced complaint reporting capacity
